description: Establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee on Human Rights
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As a member State of the United Nations, Sri Lanka is a State Party to 09 core Human Rights Treaties and 5 Optional Protocols. In addition to the said international Conventions, Sri Lanka also participates in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR), which provides Sri Lanka with the opportunity to voluntarily declare the steps taken at the national level to make progress on human rights. During Sri Lanka’s review under the 4th cycle of the UPR in 2023, Sri Lanka was given the opportunity to submit a voluntary mid-term report, outlining the progress made in implementing the recommendations received from other states, prior to the next UPR. Accordingly, the need to establish an effective multi-stakeholder national mechanism, including Ministries, Departments and Institutions of the Government, for the preparation of the said Report has been identified. As such, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism; and the Minister of Justice and National Integration to establish an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee on Human Rights to serve as a stable national framework for an effective domestic process of follow-up and reporting on human rights activities in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.
